results.correct_value: No parking fee or pass is required at Copper Glance Trailhead.

results.correct_value: About 11-12 mi round trip and about 5,600-5,800 ft of gain for Big + West Craggy (the trip the itinerary describes); 12-16 mi and a 4,500 ft floor are wrong.
results.evidence: The Mountaineers route page gives 12 mi and 5,800 ft for scrambling Big and West Craggy; HippoHamster gives 11.6 mi and 5,600 ft for the same two-day trip; trailcatjim gives ~11 mi and 5,600 ft gained/lost with a 3.3 hr / 2,800 ft day 1 to a 6,600 ft basin camp (the exact itinerary stored here). The approach's 12-16 mi and the totalNote's 10 mi / 4,500 ft are corrected; day 2 miles/gain/loss are set so the itinerary TOTAL reads 11.6 mi, 5,600 ft up and down. dist_km (6.4 km one-way) was left alone: no source gives a Big-Craggy-only one-way distance, so the one-way figure is not established.

results.correct_value: gain_ft and loss_ft 5,600 (car-to-car for the Big + West Craggy trip the itinerary describes); itinerary day 2 gain 2,800 / loss 5,600.
results.evidence: gain_ft 4,570 is below the row's own 4,668 ft net rise (3,810 ft trailhead to 8,478 ft summit), so it is impossible. Two trip reports of the same two-day Big + West Craggy trip give 5,600 ft gained (HippoHamster) and 5,600 ft gained and lost (trailcatjim), and The Mountaineers gives 5,800 ft. Day 1 is 2,800 ft, so day 2 carries the remaining 2,800 ft up and all 5,600 ft down, making the itinerary TOTAL equal gain_ft/loss_ft.

results.correct_value: Buckskin Ridge Trail over Slate Pass 0.9 mi, Whistler Cutoff down to Middle Fork Pasayten Trail #478 (~4 mi), north (downstream) along the Middle Fork, up to Fred's Lake as the usual first camp, then Rolo Pass, upper Eureka Creek and Shellrock Basin. Robinson Pass belongs to the separate, longer Robinson Creek approach.
results.evidence: WTA's Whistler Cutoff page: from the Slate Pass trailhead descend the Buckskin Ridge Trail 0.9 mi to the Whistler Cutoff, then 2.7 mi to the Middle Fork Pasayten crossing and 0.4 mi to the Robinson Creek trail (matching waypoint[1] at 4 mi). trailcatjim's Shellrock Basin/Lago/Carru/Blackcap report starts at the Buckskin Ridge Trailhead (6,900 ft), camps first at Fred's Lake (~5.1 hr from the car) and reaches Shellrock Basin via Rolo Pass and Eureka Creek; his Lost Peak loop shows Robinson Pass is the route from the Robinson Creek Trailhead on Lost River Road, then down-river past Fred's Lake. The approach prose, which crossed into the West Fork and passed Robinson Pass, is rewritten; the descent line and waypoint[2]'s 'up-valley' (the Middle Fork runs north, so the walk to Fred's Lake is down-valley) are aligned.

patches.find: From the trailhead, follow the ridge/trail over Slate Pass and drop down into the West Fork Pasayten drainage, picking up Robinson Creek/Middle Fork Pasayten Trail #478 (the full trail runs ~23 miles one-way through this country). Continue down-valley past Robinson Pass to the Middle Fork Pasayten River (roughly 9 miles in, then a further ~3-mile descent to the river) — most parties camp here or push on the first day (about 5 hours trailhead-to-camp at a backpacking pace). Day two, follow the Middle Fork Pasayten downstream, then turn up past Fred's Lake (a reliable water source and common camp) and climb to 7,100-ft Rolo Pass
patches.replace: From the trailhead, follow the Buckskin Ridge Trail over Slate Pass for about 0.9 mile, then take the Whistler Cutoff down into the Middle Fork Pasayten valley to Robinson Creek/Middle Fork Pasayten Trail #478, about 4 miles in. Follow the Middle Fork downstream (north) for about five miles, then climb to Fred's Lake, a reliable water source and the usual first-night camp (about 5 hours trailhead-to-camp at a backpacking pace). A longer alternative starts low at the Robinson Creek Trailhead on the Lost River Road and crosses Robinson Pass into the same valley. Day two, climb from Fred's Lake to 7,100-ft Rolo Pass

results.fact: Where to leave the trail for the col
results.evidence: Sources disagree with both fields and with each other: a route summary surfaced in search says to follow trail 474 east to below Shellrock Pass at about 6,400 ft and then traverse SSW below the cliffs; Country Highpoints followed the ridge southwest from a camp at Shellrock Pass to the col. Neither matches approach_variants' 7,100 ft, and the variant's claim that crossing the pass drops into Eureka Creek conflicts with the approach/waypoints (and trailcatjim) that put Eureka Creek before Shellrock Basin. Could not get 2 agreeing sources; no patch.

results.correct_value: The ~6,900 ft point is the Slate Pass (Buckskin Ridge) trailhead, not the road end; the road continues to a gate at the base of Slate Peak (summit 7,488 ft).
results.evidence: trailcatjim puts the Buckskin Ridge Trailhead on Slate Peak Road at 6,900 ft; Explore Washington says the road is gated at the base of Slate Peak (7,488 ft) with a short walk to the lookout, and Ordealist gives 3 miles from Harts Pass to Slate Peak. The waypoint's '3.5 miles to the road end at roughly 6,900 ft' is replaced (in the road-opening patch on the same string) by wording that places the trailhead below the gate and drops the unsourced 3.5 mi. road.driveNote's '3 more miles to Slate Peak (7,488 ft)' matches Ordealist and is left; the bivy note's 7,440 ft gate is bivy-owned and unverified.
